newsitem.title: GREECE: MINOAN INVESTS $210MLN IN TWO NEW HIGHSPEED VESSELS.
newsitem.headline: MINOAN INVESTS $210MLN IN TWO NEW HIGHSPEED VESSELS.

text.p: Minoan Lines will launch two new highspeed ferries by mid-1998 at the cost of $210 million, an addition to its fleet of six ships now covering the Italy-Greece route, it said on Friday.
The two new ships, Ikarus and Pasiphae, will be constructed in Sweden and will make their maiden trips on January and June 1998, respectively.

Their total cost is budgeted at $ 210 million. It will be financed by equity capital -- 30 percent -- and is the biggest investment ever made on two ships, by a Greek passenger shipping company, it said.
Ikarus' construction is proceeding at a fast rate and it should be delivered to Minoan in mid-December of this year.
Its cost is estimated at $ 105 million and its speed will be 27 knots. Ikarus will transport 1,200 passengers and 150 trucks or 1,000 cars between Greece and Italy, the statement said.

The two new ferries, along with the company's most recent one, Aretousa, will have a combined capacity of 50,000 passengers and 4,000 trucks or 25,000 cars on a weekly basis. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
